headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict from shared filesystem plus broad egress; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and Flowise reads/writes server filesystem and uploaded files, so content can cross from one agent into the other through shared files. Flowise’s graph-based tools-as-nodes can treat file content as flow input, making instruction smuggling plausible. Dexter’s autonomous execution increases the chance it emits untrusted content that Flowise may ingest.
conditions: IF Dexter writes attacker-controlled text into .dexter/scratchpad/ and Flowise ingests that file in a flow, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace, file-mediated instruction bridging exists.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of scratchpad files into Flowise flows.
Add a manual review step before Flowise consumes Dexter outputs.
Prefix/escape file content before passing it between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; Flowise reads and writes server filesystem and uploads files, and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive data can move from Dexter into Flowise and then out through model providers or configured HTTP tools. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default deployments.
conditions: IF Dexter stores financial data in shared files and Flowise loads those files, sensitive data can be exposed.
IF Flowise flows send uploaded file contents to model providers or HTTP tools, leakage can extend beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Use separate storage locations for each agent.
Restrict Flowise flows from reading Dexter scratchpad files.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after shared-run testing.
Limit Flowise tool nodes to non-network actions for shared data.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while Flowise supports multiple instances with shared state via server datastore and can write the filesystem. Even though Flowise cannot modify git state, overlapping writes to shared files or datastore can still race and corrupt work products. The interaction is plausible in default deployments unless the operator isolates state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Dexter and Flowise run simultaneously in one deployment, shared-state races are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with an external lock.
Disable concurrent runs during shared-resource updates.
Keep Flowise from writing into Dexter-managed paths.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared datastore updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can generate outputs from APIs, while Flowise builds graph-based flows that can treat upstream outputs as node inputs. If Flowise consumes Dexter’s results without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Dexter outputs as authoritative node inputs, downstream actions may propagate errors.
IF a flow triggers model-provider or HTTP tools based on Dexter output, the cascade can affect external systems.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before downstream actions.
Require schema validation on Dexter outputs.
Compare Dexter outputs against a second source before acting.
Disable auto-execution of flows fed by Dexter.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and can store uploaded files on the server filesystem. If the pair is used on regulated financial records, retention and residency controls may diverge because neither profile documents matching compliance guarantees. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are routed through both agents, retention and logging policies must align.
IF Flowise stores uploaded files containing financial data, compliance scope expands beyond Dexter alone.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated records through the pair.
Review retention settings in Flowise before use.
Delete shared files after each run.
Restrict access to financial datasets to one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a common compliance policy.
